items.stem: Complete the statement: In a consignment, the consignor is …
options: the agent who sells the goods
the owner who sends the goods to an agent to sell
the carrier who transports the goods
items.answer: the owner who sends the goods to an agent to sell
items.markingKey: Consignor = principal/owner; consignee = agent [1].

items.stem: Explain why goods sent on consignment are not recorded as sales by the consignor.
items.answer: Ownership does not pass to the consignee; the consignee is only an agent. A sale occurs when the consignee sells to a third party.
items.markingKey: No transfer of ownership [1]; sale when agent sells [1] [2]

items.stem: Explain the purpose of a proforma invoice in a consignment.
items.answer: It informs the consignee of the goods sent and the expected selling price; it is not a demand for payment and no entry is made in the consignee's ledger.
items.markingKey: Information/price guide [1]; not a sale/no ledger entry [1] [2]

items.stem: Isla of Cape Town sent 500 ceramic vases costing $30 each on consignment to Ana. Isla paid freight of $1,000 and insurance of $1,900. Ana paid import duty of $3,600 and selling expenses of $1,400. Ana sold 250 vases at $60 each and is entitled to commission of 10% on sales. Calculate the value of the unsold inventory and the profit on consignment in the books of Isla.
items.answer: Unsold inventory $10,750; profit $1,350

items.stem: Jonas of Toronto sent 1,000 mountain bicycles costing $180 each on consignment to Hana. Jonas paid freight of $5,400 and insurance of $1,700. Hana paid import duty of $3,300 and selling expenses of $1,300. Hana sold 300 bicycles at $360 each and is entitled to commission of 8% on sales. Prepare the consignment account in the books of Jonas, showing the profit on consignment.
items.answer: Profit on consignment $40,940 (unsold inventory c/d $133,280)

items.stem: Sipho of Madrid sent 100 ceramic vases costing $30 each on consignment to Aisha. Sipho paid freight of $2,000 and insurance of $1,600. Aisha paid import duty of $3,700 and selling expenses of $1,900. Aisha sold 80 vases at $42 each and is entitled to commission of 12% on sales plus a del credere commission of 2%. (a) Calculate the value of the unsold inventory at the end of the period. (b) Calculate the amount Aisha should remit.

Answer both parts. (a) Complete the statement: Commission earned by the consignee is debited in the consignor's books to the … (b) Complete the statement: Goods sent on consignment remain the property of …
items.answer: (a) consignment account (b) the consignor until they are sold
items.markingKey: (a) Commission is an expense of the consignment [1]. (b) Ownership stays with the consignor; not a sale [1].

items.stem: Distinguish between a consignment and an ordinary credit sale.
items.answer: In a consignment, ownership and risk stay with the consignor and the agent earns commission; in a credit sale ownership passes to the buyer, who owes the price.
items.markingKey: Ownership/risk [1]; agent commission vs buyer debt [1] [2]

items.stem: Jonas sent 1000 mountain bicycles costing $150,000 to an agent, Daniel, on consignment, and the bookkeeper recorded the full amount as a credit sale to Daniel. Explain the error and its effect on revenue and on inventory.
items.answer: Goods on consignment are not sold until the agent sells them; revenue is overstated (by the invoiced value) and inventory understated — unsold goods should remain in Jonas's inventory at cost plus non-recurring expenses.
items.markingKey: Ownership remains with consignor [1]; revenue/receivables overstated [1]; inventory of unsold goods omitted [1] [3]

items.stem: Ines sent 250 cases of olive oil costing $10,000 to an agent, Ethan, on consignment, and the bookkeeper recorded the full amount as a credit sale to Ethan. Explain the error and its effect on revenue and on inventory.
items.answer: Goods on consignment are not sold until the agent sells them; revenue is overstated (by the invoiced value) and inventory understated — unsold goods should remain in Ines's inventory at cost plus non-recurring expenses.
items.markingKey: Ownership remains with consignor [1]; revenue/receivables overstated [1]; inventory of unsold goods omitted [1] [3]

items.stem: Ana of Doha sent 1,000 water pumps costing $200 each on consignment to Amara. Ana paid freight of $600 and insurance of $300. Amara paid import duty of $900 and selling expenses of $2,200. Amara sold 800 pumps at $320 each and is entitled to commission of 12% on sales. Amara remits the balance due by bank transfer. Prepare Ana's account in the books of Amara and calculate the amount remitted.
items.answer: Amount remitted $222,180
items.markingKey: Cr sales $256,000 [1]; Dr expenses paid duty $900 + selling $2,200 [1]; Dr commission $30,720 [1]; balance remitted $222,180 [1]

items.stem: Ethan of Nairobi sent 250 bags of coffee beans costing $50 each on consignment to Ana. Ethan paid freight of $4,300 and insurance of $1,700. Ana paid import duty of $2,900 and selling expenses of $300. Ana sold 175 bags at $70 each and is entitled to commission of 12% on sales plus a del credere commission of 2%. Ana remits the balance due by bank transfer. Prepare Ethan's account in the books of Ana and calculate the amount remitted.
items.answer: Amount remitted $7,335
items.markingKey: Cr sales $12,250 [1]; Dr expenses paid duty $2,900 + selling $300 [1]; Dr commission $1,715 [1]; balance remitted $7,335 [1]

items.stem: Noah of Doha sent 1,000 mountain bicycles costing $120 each on consignment to Ethan. Noah paid freight of $3,600 and insurance of $2,000. Ethan paid import duty of $2,200 and selling expenses of $2,200. Ethan sold 700 bicycles at $240 each and is entitled to commission of 5% on sales. Prepare the consignment account in the books of Noah, showing the profit on consignment.
items.answer: Profit on consignment $67,940 (unsold inventory c/d $38,340)

items.stem: Mateo of Auckland sent 1,000 solar lanterns costing $20 each on consignment to Lucas. Mateo paid freight of $2,700 and insurance of $1,800. Lucas paid import duty of $2,800 and selling expenses of $2,300. Lucas sold 700 units at $28 each and is entitled to commission of 10% on sales plus a del credere commission of 3%. (a) Calculate the value of the unsold inventory at the end of the period. (b) Calculate the amount Lucas should remit.

Leila of Nairobi sent 200 ceramic vases costing $20 each on consignment to Nadia. Leila paid freight of $2,100 and insurance of $2,000. Nadia paid import duty of $1,200 and selling expenses of $600. Nadia sold 140 vases at $32 each and is entitled to commission of 12% on sales. (a) Calculate the value of the unsold inventory at the end of the period. (b) Calculate the commission due to Nadia. (c) Advise Leila whether to offer a del credere commission.
items.answer: (a) $2,790 (b) $538 (c) It costs extra commission but transfers the risk of bad debts on credit sales to the agent and encourages careful credit control.
items.markingKey: (a) 60/200 × ($4,000 + freight $2,100 + insurance $2,000 + duty $1,200) = $2,790 [2] (b) 12% × $4,480 [1] (c) Cost [1]; benefit: bad debts borne by agent [1]; recommendation [1] [3]

items.stem: Which expense is included when valuing unsold consignment inventory?
items.answer: Freight to the consignee's premises
items.markingKey: Non-recurring costs to bring goods to location (freight, insurance in transit, import duty) included [1].

items.stem: Explain why a proportion of freight and insurance is included in the valuation of unsold consignment inventory.
items.answer: These costs were incurred to bring all the goods to the consignee's location; under IAS 2 such costs form part of the cost of inventory, so the unsold goods carry their share.
items.markingKey: Costs to bring goods to present location [1]; IAS 2 / matching [1] [2]

items.stem: Explain why a consignee might demand a del credere commission.
items.answer: It compensates the agent for accepting the risk of bad debts on credit sales, which would otherwise fall on the consignor.
items.markingKey: Compensation for bad debt risk [1]; credit sales [1] [2]

items.stem: Tomás of Lisbon sent 250 ceramic vases costing $30 each on consignment to Sofia. Tomás paid freight of $3,600 and insurance of $1,800. Sofia paid import duty of $3,400 and selling expenses of $2,400. Sofia sold 175 vases at $48 each and is entitled to commission of 10% on sales. Calculate the value of the unsold inventory held by the consignee.
items.markingKey: Cost of goods $7,500 + freight $3,600 + insurance $1,800 + duty $3,400 = $16,300 [1]; × 75/250 = $4,890 [1]; selling expenses excluded [1]

items.stem: Grace of Cape Town sent 250 rolls of batik cloth costing $20 each on consignment to Aisha. Grace paid freight of $4,600 and insurance of $1,300. Aisha paid import duty of $3,900 and selling expenses of $1,500. Aisha sold 125 rolls at $28 each and is entitled to commission of 10% on sales plus a del credere commission of 3%. Calculate the value of the unsold inventory held by the consignee.
items.markingKey: Cost of goods $5,000 + freight $4,600 + insurance $1,300 + duty $3,900 = $14,800 [1]; × 125/250 = $7,400 [1]; selling expenses excluded [1]

items.stem: Chloe of Toronto sent 800 ceramic vases costing $30 each on consignment to Ana. Chloe paid freight of $500 and insurance of $1,700. Ana paid import duty of $3,500 and selling expenses of $2,500. Ana sold 480 vases at $48 each and is entitled to commission of 8% on sales plus a del credere commission of 3%. items.answer: (a) $2,534 (b) It costs extra commission but transfers the risk of bad debts on credit sales to the agent and encourages careful credit control.
items.markingKey: (a) 11% × $23,040 [1] (b) Cost [1]; benefit: bad debts borne by agent [1]; recommendation [1] [3]

items.stem: Complete the statement: A del credere commission is paid to the consignee in return for …
options: storing the goods free of charge
bearing any bad debts on credit sales
items.answer: bearing any bad debts on credit sales
items.markingKey: Del credere agent guarantees payment by credit customers [1].

items.stem: Kwame consigned 100 cartons of tea costing $2,000; freight and insurance were $2,600, selling expenses $1,500 and commission $180. 50 cartons were unsold. A trainee valued them at $3,140. Explain the error and calculate the correct value.
items.answer: Selling expenses and commission relate to goods sold and must be excluded. Correct value 50/100 × $4,600 = $2,300.
items.markingKey: Exclude recurring/selling costs and commission [1]; include non-recurring costs [1]; correct value $2,300 [1] [3]

items.stem: Ravi consigned 800 rolls of batik cloth costing $20,000; freight and insurance were $2,000, import duty $3,900, selling expenses $2,000 and commission $3,200. 160 rolls were unsold. A trainee valued them at $6,220. Explain the error and calculate the correct value.
items.answer: Selling expenses and commission relate to goods sold and must be excluded. Correct value 160/800 × $25,900 = $5,180.
items.markingKey: Exclude recurring/selling costs and commission [1]; include non-recurring costs [1]; correct value $5,180 [1] [3]

items.stem: Leila consigned 500 rolls of batik cloth costing $22,500; freight and insurance were $3,800, import duty $900, selling expenses $800 and commission $5,400. 100 rolls were unsold. A trainee valued them at $6,680. Explain the error and calculate the correct value.
items.answer: Selling expenses and commission relate to goods sold and must be excluded. Correct value 100/500 × $27,200 = $5,440.
items.markingKey: Exclude recurring/selling costs and commission [1]; include non-recurring costs [1]; correct value $5,440 [1] [3]

items.stem: Priya of Lisbon sent 400 leather jackets costing $80 each on consignment to Amara. Priya paid freight of $5,400 and insurance of $700. Amara paid selling expenses of $2,800. Amara sold 360 jackets at $120 each and is entitled to commission of 8% on sales. What is the value of the unsold inventory?
items.markingKey: Cost of goods $32,000 + freight $5,400 + insurance $700 = $38,100 [1]; × 40/400 = $3,810 [1]; selling expenses excluded [1]

items.stem: Freya sells goods on consignment and earns 5% commission on all sales plus a del credere commission of 2.5% on all sales. Sales were $137,000, of which 60% were on credit; one credit customer owing $2,200 became insolvent. Calculate the total commission and state who bears the bad debt.
items.answer: Commission $10,275; the bad debt of $2,200 is borne by Freya (del credere agent)
items.markingKey: 5% × $137,000 = $6,850 [1]; del credere 2.5% = $3,425 [1]; total $10,275 [1]; bad debt borne by consignee [1]

items.stem: Mohammed sells goods on consignment and earns 5% commission on all sales plus a del credere commission of 2% on all sales. Sales were $121,000, of which 50% were on credit; one credit customer owing $1,700 became insolvent. Calculate the total commission and state who bears the bad debt.
items.answer: Commission $8,470; the bad debt of $1,700 is borne by Mohammed (del credere agent)
items.markingKey: 5% × $121,000 = $6,050 [1]; del credere 2% = $2,420 [1]; total $8,470 [1]; bad debt borne by consignee [1]

items.stem: Elena of Dubai sent 250 solar lanterns costing $30 each on consignment to Grace. Elena paid freight of $4,700 and insurance of $800. Grace paid import duty of $500 and selling expenses of $2,900. Grace sold 200 units at $52 each and is entitled to commission of 5% on sales plus a del credere commission of 3%. (a) Calculate the amount Grace should remit. (b) Explain why selling expenses are not included in the value of unsold inventory.
items.answer: (a) $6,168 (b) Selling expenses relate to goods already sold; only costs of bringing the goods to their present location and condition (IAS 2) are included.

items.stem: Ines of Kuala Lumpur sent 1,000 ceramic vases costing $20 each on consignment to Mateo. Ines paid freight of $5,000 and insurance of $1,600. Mateo paid import duty of $3,400 and selling expenses of $1,600. Mateo sold 800 vases at $30 each and is entitled to commission of 5% on sales plus a del credere commission of 3%. (a) Calculate the value of the unsold inventory at the end of the period. (b) Advise Ines whether to offer a del credere commission.
items.answer: (a) $6,000 (b) It costs extra commission but transfers the risk of bad debts on credit sales to the agent and encourages careful credit control.
items.markingKey: (a) 200/1000 × ($20,000 + freight $5,000 + insurance $1,600 + duty $3,400) = $6,000 [2] (b) Cost [1]; benefit: bad debts borne by agent [1]; recommendation [1] [3]

items.stem: Complete the statement: A memorandum joint venture account is used to …
options: show the capital of each venturer
calculate the total profit or loss of the joint venture
record the cash paid between venturers
items.answer: calculate the total profit or loss of the joint venture
items.markingKey: Combines all venturers' transactions to find profit; not part of double entry [1].

items.stem: Complete the statement: In each venturer's own books, the joint venture account records …
options: only the sales of the venture
only the transactions carried out by that venturer, plus his share of profit
items.answer: only the transactions carried out by that venturer, plus his share of profit
items.markingKey: Own JV account: own expenses, own sales, own share of profit [1].

items.stem: Explain why the memorandum joint venture account is not part of the double-entry system.
items.answer: Each venturer records only his own transactions in his own books; the memorandum account merely combines the figures to calculate profit, so it is prepared outside the ledgers.
items.markingKey: Each venturer keeps own records [1]; memorandum combines for profit only [1] [2]

items.stem: Noah and Leila agreed to organise a trade fair in Dubai, sharing profits 1:1. Noah paid expenses of $69,600 and received sales of $58,000; Leila paid expenses of $15,800 and received sales of $42,600. Calculate the profit on the joint venture and each venturer's share.
items.answer: Profit $15,200: Noah $7,600, Leila $7,600
items.markingKey: Memorandum JV: sales $100,600 − expenses $85,400 = profit $15,200 [1]; shares Noah $7,600, Leila $7,600 [1]; Noah's JV account: $69,600 + $7,600 − $58,000 = $19,200 Dr (due to Noah) [1]

items.stem: Felix and Ravi entered a joint venture to sell mobile phones, sharing profits 1:1. Felix bought goods for $37,000 and paid transport of $1,900; Ravi paid advertising of $2,100. Felix received sales of $20,500 and Ravi received sales of $46,100. At the end, Felix took the remaining goods for his own use at an agreed value of $3,000. (a) State the amount and direction of the final settlement. (b) Explain how the goods taken by Felix are treated.
items.answer: (a) Ravi pays Felix $29,700 (b) Treated as a sale to Felix: credit the JV accounts with $3,000, so the venture is credited and Felix's balance due falls.

items.stem: Explain two advantages of a joint venture for two businesses.
items.answer: Shares risk and cost of a one-off project; combines expertise or resources; no permanent commitment; access to new markets.
items.markingKey: Two advantages [1 each] + explanation [1 each] [4]

items.stem: Arjun and Hana agreed to stage a music festival, sharing profits 3:2. Arjun paid expenses of $44,300 and received sales of $8,500; Hana paid expenses of $8,100 and received sales of $72,400. Calculate the profit on the joint venture and each venturer's share.
items.markingKey: Memorandum JV: sales $80,900 − expenses $52,400 = profit $28,500 [1]; shares Arjun $17,100, Hana $11,400 [1]; Arjun's JV account: $44,300 + $17,100 − $8,500 = $52,900 Dr (due to Arjun) [1]

items.stem: In a joint venture with Sipho, Samuel paid expenses of $7,900 and Sipho received all the sales of $53,400. Samuel recorded both the expenses and Sipho's sales in his own joint venture account and treated the balance as profit. Explain the error.

items.markingKey: Own transactions only [1]; profit from memorandum account [1]; balance represents amount due, not profit [1] [3]

items.markingKey: Dr Consignment to [agent], Cr Goods sent on consignment [1].

items.stem: Ana sent 100 leather jackets costing $5,000 to an agent, Lucas, on consignment, and the bookkeeper recorded the full amount as a credit sale to Lucas. Explain the error and its effect on revenue and on inventory.
items.answer: Goods on consignment are not sold until the agent sells them; revenue is overstated (by the invoiced value) and inventory understated — unsold goods should remain in Ana's inventory at cost plus non-recurring expenses.
items.markingKey: Ownership remains with consignor [1]; revenue/receivables overstated [1]; inventory of unsold goods omitted [1] [3]

items.stem: Give a reason for each answer. (a) Explain why goods sent on consignment are not recorded as sales by the consignor. (b) Explain the purpose of a proforma invoice in a consignment.
items.answer: (a) Ownership does not pass to the consignee; the consignee is only an agent. A sale occurs when the consignee sells to a third party. (b) It informs the consignee of the goods sent and the expected selling price; it is not a demand for payment and no entry is made in the consignee's ledger.
items.markingKey: (a) No transfer of ownership [1]; sale when agent sells [1] [2] (b) Information/price guide [1]; not a sale/no ledger entry [1] [2]

items.stem: Hana of Singapore sent 400 carved teak chairs costing $60 each on consignment to Lucas. Hana paid freight of $5,700 and insurance of $1,100. Lucas paid import duty of $1,800 and selling expenses of $3,000. Lucas sold 200 chairs at $90 each and is entitled to commission of 8% on sales. Lucas remits the balance due by bank transfer. Prepare Hana's account in the books of Lucas and calculate the amount remitted.
items.answer: Amount remitted $11,760
items.markingKey: Cr sales $18,000 [1]; Dr expenses paid duty $1,800 + selling $3,000 [1]; Dr commission $1,440 [1]; balance remitted $11,760 [1]

items.stem: Mateo of Cape Town sent 200 ceramic vases costing $50 each on consignment to Sofia. Mateo paid freight of $500 and insurance of $1,400. Sofia paid import duty of $3,700 and selling expenses of $2,900. Sofia sold 160 vases at $88 each and is entitled to commission of 5% on sales plus a del credere commission of 3%. Prepare the consignment account in the books of Mateo, showing the profit on consignment.
items.answer: Profit on consignment -$2,426 (unsold inventory c/d $3,120)

items.stem: Mateo of Nairobi sent 100 cartons of tea costing $40 each on consignment to Tomás. Mateo paid freight of $4,900 and insurance of $500. Tomás paid import duty of $400 and selling expenses of $2,300. Tomás sold 80 cartons at $56 each and is entitled to commission of 12% on sales. (a) Calculate the value of the unsold inventory at the end of the period. (b) Advise Mateo whether to offer a del credere commission.
items.answer: (a) $1,960 (b) It costs extra commission but transfers the risk of bad debts on credit sales to the agent and encourages careful credit control.
items.markingKey: (a) 20/100 × ($4,000 + freight $4,900 + insurance $500 + duty $400) = $1,960 [2] (b) Cost [1]; benefit: bad debts borne by agent [1]; recommendation [1] [3]

items.stem: Answer both parts. (a) Complete the statement: Recurring expenses such as the consignee's selling costs are … (b) Complete the statement: A del credere commission is paid to the consignee in return for …
items.answer: (a) charged against the consignment profit and excluded from unsold inventory (b) bearing any bad debts on credit sales
items.markingKey: (a) Selling costs relate to sold goods [1]. (b) Del credere agent guarantees payment by credit customers [1].

items.stem: Daniel consigned 400 water pumps costing $48,000; freight and insurance were $3,500, import duty $2,800, selling expenses $2,900 and commission $4,032. 160 pumps were unsold. A trainee valued them at $24,493. Explain the error and calculate the correct value.
items.answer: Selling expenses and commission relate to goods sold and must be excluded. Correct value 160/400 × $54,300 = $21,720.
items.markingKey: Exclude recurring/selling costs and commission [1]; include non-recurring costs [1]; correct value $21,720 [1] [3]

items.stem: Zara of Nairobi sent 250 bags of coffee beans costing $60 each on consignment to Hana. Zara paid freight of $4,600 and insurance of $1,200. Hana paid import duty of $2,000 and selling expenses of $900. Hana sold 150 bags at $90 each and is entitled to commission of 5% on sales. Calculate the value of the unsold inventory held by the consignee.
items.markingKey: Cost of goods $15,000 + freight $4,600 + insurance $1,200 + duty $2,000 = $22,800 [1]; × 100/250 = $9,120 [1]; selling expenses excluded [1]

items.stem: Mateo sells goods on consignment and earns 5% commission on all sales plus a del credere commission of 2.5% on all sales. Sales were $198,000, of which 50% were on credit; one credit customer owing $3,800 became insolvent. Calculate the total commission and state who bears the bad debt.
items.answer: Commission $14,850; the bad debt of $3,800 is borne by Mateo (del credere agent)
items.markingKey: 5% × $198,000 = $9,900 [1]; del credere 2.5% = $4,950 [1]; total $14,850 [1]; bad debt borne by consignee [1]

items.stem: Freya of Lisbon sent 250 rolls of batik cloth costing $20 each on consignment to Ana. Freya paid freight of $4,900 and insurance of $1,100. Ana paid import duty of $3,800 and selling expenses of $2,700. Ana sold 150 rolls at $35 each and is entitled to commission of 10% on sales plus a del credere commission of 3%. (a) Calculate the commission due to Ana. (b) Advise Freya whether to offer a del credere commission.
items.answer: (a) $683 (b) It costs extra commission but transfers the risk of bad debts on credit sales to the agent and encourages careful credit control.
items.markingKey: (a) 13% × $5,250 [1] (b) Cost [1]; benefit: bad debts borne by agent [1]; recommendation [1] [3]

items.stem: In a joint venture with Tomás, Tariq paid expenses of $14,500 and Tomás received all the sales of $30,400. Tariq recorded both the expenses and Tomás's sales in his own joint venture account and treated the balance as profit. Explain the error.
items.answer: Tariq's joint venture account should record only Tariq's own transactions (expenses $14,500) and his share of profit; Tomás's sales belong in the memorandum JV account, which is used to calculate profit.
items.markingKey: Own transactions only [1]; profit from memorandum account [1]; balance represents amount due, not profit [1] [3]

items.stem: In a joint venture with Mohammed, Yusuf paid expenses of $32,600 and Mohammed received all the sales of $12,700. Yusuf recorded both the expenses and Mohammed's sales in his own joint venture account and treated the balance as profit. Explain the error.
items.answer: Yusuf's joint venture account should record only Yusuf's own transactions (expenses $32,600) and his share of profit; Mohammed's sales belong in the memorandum JV account, which is used to calculate profit.
items.markingKey: Own transactions only [1]; profit from memorandum account [1]; balance represents amount due, not profit [1] [3]

items.stem: Sipho and Elena agreed to import and sell a batch of laptops, sharing profits 3:1. Sipho paid expenses of $64,700 and received sales of $47,300; Elena paid expenses of $9,800 and received sales of $106,800. Calculate the profit on the joint venture and each venturer's share.
items.answer: Profit $79,600: Sipho $59,700, Elena $19,900
items.markingKey: Memorandum JV: sales $154,100 − expenses $74,500 = profit $79,600 [1]; shares Sipho $59,700, Elena $19,900 [1]; Sipho's JV account: $64,700 + $59,700 − $47,300 = $77,100 Dr (due to Sipho) [1]

items.stem: Aisha and Ines entered a joint venture to sell handmade rugs, sharing profits 1:1. Aisha bought goods for $59,000 and paid transport of $3,300; Ines paid advertising of $1,700. Aisha received sales of $47,000 and Ines received sales of $59,600. At the end, Aisha took the remaining goods for his own use at an agreed value of $3,400. (a) Prepare the joint venture with Ines account in Aisha's books. (b) State the amount and direction of the final settlement.
items.answer: (a) Balance $34,900; Ines pays Aisha $34,900 (b) Ines pays Aisha $34,900
items.markingKey: (a) Dr goods, transport, profit share $23,000; Cr sales $47,000, goods taken $3,400 [2]; balance $34,900 [1] [3] (b) [1]
